pr_title: Add GH_HOST to hosts list if it has corresponding auth token
pr_body:
This PR changes the behavior of `envConfig.Hosts()` to now include in the return set `GH_HOST` if it has a corresponding authentication token from one of the numerous environment variable token locations. This solves the case where `auth` commands were displaying that a user was not authenticated despite having both `GH_HOST` and a corresponding authentication token environment variable set. 

Closes https://github.com/cli/cli/issues/4576

issue_context.title: auth status shows "not logged into any GitHub hosts" even with GH_ENTERPRISE_TOKEN and GH_HOST
issue_context.body:
### Describe the bug

gh version 2.1.0

Not logged in with GH_ENTERPRISE_TOKEN and GH_HOST set

### Steps to reproduce the behavior
1. Set both GH_ENTERPRISE_TOKEN and GH_HOST environment variables
2. from cmd, type `gh auth status`

### Expected vs actual behavior
Expected: Signed in to github enterprise host
Actual: Not logged in

Additionally: When attempting to sign in with `gh auth login --hostname %GH_HOST%` with be blocked due to GH_ENTERPRISE_TOKEN in use message despite being signed out

### Logs
```C:\>gh auth status
You are not logged into any GitHub hosts. Run gh auth login to authenticate.

C:\>gh auth login --hostname %GH_HOST%
The value of the GH_ENTERPRISE_TOKEN environment variable is being used for authentication.
To have GitHub CLI store credentials instead, first clear the value from the environment.```
comments:
> Expected: Signed in to github enterprise host
> Actual: Not logged in

Obvious question, but: did you set a valid authentication token as GH_ENTERPRISE_TOKEN?

> Additionally: When attempting to sign in with `gh auth login --hostname %GH_HOST%` with be blocked due to GH_ENTERPRISE_TOKEN in use message despite being signed out

This is expected. `gh auth login` is a flow that logs you in and stores the gh token internally. However, that whole authentication is overridden if there is a GH_ENTERPRISE_TOKEN, and since gh cannot override an environment variable, it's telling you that you either have to fix the token in GH_ENTERPRISE_TOKEN or remove the variable entirely and instead authenticate with `gh auth login` flow. Please try either of the approaches and tell us how it went!

I can confirm the token is valid. I may sign in if I remove the environment variables and use `gh auth login --hostname <hostname> --with-token` using the same token on standard input.

While manual sign in works, I am looking for the GH_ENTERPRISE_TOKEN solution as this flow will be use on automated CI/CD with VM image

I've just tried to reproduce with a token I've generated on a Enterprise instance:
```
$ GH_ENTERPRISE_TOKEN="..." GH_HOST=example.com gh auth status
example.com
  ✓ Logged in to example.com as mislav (GH_ENTERPRISE_TOKEN)
  ✓ Git operations for example.com configured to use https protocol.
  ✓ Token: *******************
```
All gh operations work with this token. What is the output that you get, and can you manually confirm that your token is valid? Does the token include `repo, read:org` scopes?
```
curl -i https://example.com/api/v3/user -H "Authorization: token YOURTOKEN"
```

the scopes I gave is:
- repo
- workflow
- read:org
- read:repo_hook
- notifications

actually, I would like to note that originally, I also have GH_TOKEN (all three GH_TOKEN, GH_HOST, and GH_ENTERPRISE_TOKEN) set and that only the github.com login successfully.

note: ~\AppData\Roaming\GitHub CLI\hosts.yml is blank

@joeksy The scopes look good. Can you run a manual curl request and double-check if the token is valid? 
```
curl -si "https://$GH_HOST/api/v3/user" -H "Authorization: token $GH_ENTERPRISE_TOKEN" | grep -i '^\(HTTP\|X-OAuth-Scopes\)'
```

> note: ~\AppData\Roaming\GitHub CLI\hosts.yml is blank

The hosts config file is expected to be blank if you're using `*_TOKEN` environment variables. Whenever these variables are present, they are used instead of anything in `hosts.yml`.

gh auth status returns 
`You are not logged into any GitHub hosts. Run gh auth login to authenticate.`

and the `grep -i ^x-oauth-scopes` returns
`x-oauth-scopes: notifications, read:org, read:repo_hook, repo, workflow`

Thanks
(then my problem is likely something else)

I manage to verify it on my local machine (not VM) that the enterprise login is indeed working.

@joeksy Please let us know if you have any problem using other gh commands with your Enterprise instance. You are welcome to open new issues for that, since this issue is now only about the `gh auth status` messaging problem.

I just want to let you know that my problem been resolved.
It turns out that somehow, in my VM image .git/config, the remote url has a `\n` a the end.
`git remote -v` return correct results, but gh commands will fail and return `no git remotes found`

I have no idea how the \n came to be. I am using a inhouse equivalent of Docker.

review_comments: Before this change, adding `ghinstance.Default()` to the list was explicitly done by _prepend_ operation. After your change, it changed to append (since that's the only operation available to us via `set`). Could we restore the prepend behavior by working with string slices just for this bit?
`stringSet.ToSlice()` was returning `[]string(nil)` when the set was empty without this change.
